title: Republish core-lib built with Kotlin 2.3.x / kotlinx-datetime 0.7.x
description: core-lib 1.1.0 is built with kotlinx-datetime 0.6.x. When the WeatherConditions app upgraded to Kotlin 2.3.20 (datetime 0.7.1), ClockHelper.now() threw NoSuchMethodError at runtime: kotlinx.datetime.Instant became a typealias of kotlin.time.Instant, so the app compiled fine but the published bytecode still returns the old type. That broke :composeApp:testReleaseUnitTest and blocked the Android release, forcing the app-side upgrade to be reverted (WeatherConditions we-cg4). The app cannot move to Kotlin 2.3.x until core-lib is rebuilt+republished against the new datetime.
acceptance_criteria: core-lib published at a new version built with Kotlin 2.3.x + datetime 0.7.x; WeatherConditions app upgraded to 2.3.x with :composeApp:testReleaseUnitTest green; any other libs exposing datetime/Instant in their public API audited the same way.
notes: DONE: core-lib 2.0.0 published (Kotlin 2.3.20 + kotlinx-datetime 0.7.1). Public API migrated off the deprecated alias to kotlin.time.Instant (Clock.now, ClockHelper.now, DogWalkingScorer + tests); zero kotlinx.datetime refs remain. Major bump because Clock.now()'s bytecode return type changed. Verified: CI green, publishToMavenLocal built all 11 targets, and all target artifacts confirmed present on GPR after publish (no partial). Added a publishToMavenLocal compile-gate to release.yaml first, since 11 immutable publications is a large poisoning surface. FOLLOW-ON: the audit showed core-lib alone does NOT unblock we-cg4 — bluetooth-lib also needed rebuilding (1.2.0, in flight).
